# Hivelore

> Executable team guardrails for coding agents. A repository's rules and lessons live in `.ai/` and are
> enforced deterministically: sensors refuse a commit that reintroduces a known mistake, command guards
> deny a forbidden agent command before it runs, checklists require a stated verification. Local files,
> no account, no LLM in the loop. CLI `@hivelore/cli`, MCP server bundled (`hivelore mcp --stdio`).

## When an agent should use it

- The developer corrects you with a lasting rule → record it (`hivelore memory add --type convention --rule "…"`) and arm it (`hivelore rules arm`).
- CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md lists rules ("NEVER…") → `npx @hivelore/cli rules audit` shows which nothing enforces (read-only, no install); `hivelore rules arm --apply` turns them into checks.
- Before changing unfamiliar code → `hivelore why <file>:<line>`: rules, sensors, doc warnings, past fixes.
- CI is red → `hivelore ci why`: failing steps and tests, infrastructure causes, memories that saw it before.
- Finishing a task → `hivelore enforce finish`; `hivelore memory propose` lists lessons derived from the branch.

## Install

- Claude Code plugin: `/plugin marketplace add Doucs91/hivelore` then `/plugin install hivelore@hivelore`
- Any agent: `npx @hivelore/cli init` (reversible; writes `.ai/`, hooks and bridge files)
